literal: Even than ambrosia, exceedingly sweet indeed is their own children's small hand stirred gruel.
translation: The simple gruel stirred by the tiny hands of one's own children is far sweeter than even the nectar of immortality.
modern: தம்முடைய பிள்ளைகளின் சிறிய கைகளால் துழாவப்பட்ட கூழானது, தேவாமிர்தத்தை விட மிகவும் இனிமையானதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet beautifully captures the joy of parenthood through a simple domestic image. It states that ordinary food or gruel (கூழ்) becomes sweeter than the legendary nectar of immortality (அமிழ்து) when it has been dabbled in by the tiny hands of one's own children. The word 'அளாவிய' suggests the messy, playful way a child mixes food with their hands. The poet uses the contrast between the grandest divine food ('அமிழ்து') and the simplest earthly food ('கூழ்') to show how parental love elevates the mundane into something sublime.
